newsitem.title: ITALY: Air One expands in Italy, buys Noman's slots.
newsitem.headline: Air One expands in Italy, buys Noman's slots.

text.p: Independent Italian carrier Air One said on Friday it had bought three slots from Noman airline, calling the move a first step in the restructuring of the country's domestic air market.

Air One, which has proven a tough competitor to ailing state carrier Alitalia since opening in November 1995, said it would take over Noman's Milan-Palermo and Rome-Olbia and Rome-Milan slots. It gave no figures for the deal.
The Rome slots were at the city's second airport, Ciampino.
"This is the first step in the rationalisation of the Italian air transport system," said Air One chairman Carlo Toto.
"Unfortunately, it's a system in which there are hostile situations and behaviour against new initiatives, despite the considerable amount of work that has so far been carried out," Toto added.

Last month, the national anti-trust authority fined flag carrier Alitalia 415 million lire ($277,000), ruling it had "impeded, blocked and restricted" the arrival of new national airlines into the market, including Air One.

Air One, which has eight Boeing 737s and plans to increase its fleet soon, said in a statement it had carried some 700,000 passengers in 1996 and had a 25 percent share of the lucrative Rome-Milan route.
The company, which also flies between Rome and the southern port Bari, last September launched flights between Rome and Turin and Naples and Milan as part of its expansion strategy.
Noman, which like Air One offered lower prices than Alitalia, started up in January 1996 and had announced it had managed to break even after just four months in business.
